items.title: Dog capture followed SOP, says Klang mayor
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Royal Klang City Council (MBDK) has denied breaching standard operating procedures (SOPs) during a stray dog capture operation that resulted in the death of a dog at Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Klang, last week. Mayor Datuk Abd Hamid Hussain said the incident occurred after a person claiming to be the dog's owner disrupted the operation. We use loops or nets to capture stray dogs.

items.title: BN 'stabbed' PH in Negri Sembilan election, says Mujahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The outcome of the Negri Sembilan election represents a triumph of racial identity politics over the multiracial, values-based platform championed by Pakatan Harapan, Amanah deputy president and election director Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa said. The result unseated the PH state government, which had been in power since 2018. Mujahid also criticised BN, PH's partner in the federal unity government, over its cooperation with PN during the state election.

items.title: Lorry driver and wife plead not guilty as Melaka court hears child abuse charges
items.summary: The accused were charged separately before Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah. Deputy public prosecutor Nor Asnini Kamarudin offered bail of RM20,000 with an additional condition that the accused not interfere with prosecution witnesses, particularly the victim. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Qayyum Ramlan offered bail of RM20,000 with the additional condition that the accused not interfere with prosecution witnesses, particularly the victim.

items.title: Sabah records RM105.5 billion trade in 2025 despite global headwinds - DOSM
items.summary: Exports fell 5.9 per cent to RM57.7 billion from RM61.3 billion in 2024, while imports rose 2.8 per cent to RM47.8 billion from RM46.4 billion. Sabah recorded a trade surplus of RM9.9 billion, although it was 33.3 per cent lower than the RM14.9 billion recorded in 2024. Crude petroleum remained Sabah's top export commodity, valued at RM17.1 billion or 29.7 per cent of total exports, followed by palm oil at RM16.8 billion (29.2 per cent) and liquefied natural gas at RM4.6 billion (8.1 per cent).

items.title: Singaporean biker killed, two fellow riders hurt in crash involving Toyota Vellfire on North-South Expressway near Kulai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A 56-year-old Singaporean motorcyclist was killed and two Malaysian riders injured in a four-vehicle crash on the North-South Expressway near Kulai yesterday. Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said preliminary investigations found that the three riders — the Singaporean and two Malaysians aged 57 and 39 — were travelling south when the crash occurred. “The incident also involved the other two motorcyclists.

items.title: MetMalaysia alert: Torrential rain, lightning and gusty winds batter states from Kedah to Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected to affect eight states and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Sik and Baling in Kedah; Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Jeli, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan; and Besut, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu. In Sarawak and Sarawak, the affected areas are Kuching (Bau), Sri Aman, Betong (Pusa and Betong), Sarikei (Pakan, Julau and Meradong), Sibu and Kapit (Song and Kapit), and the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Keningau and Tambunan), the West Coast and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

items.title: Azalina: FOI Bill to undergo clause-by-clause review
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Parliamentary Special Select Committee reviewing the Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill 2026 aims to complete its deliberations and submit recommendations before the next Dewan Rakyat sitting. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the bipartisan committee would begin its work tomorrow, with the scope of the Bill among issues expected to be scrutinised. She said the committee would first determine its terms of reference before conducting a clause-by-clause review of the Bill.

items.title: 1MDB alleges Najib orchestrated US$5.64bil fraud as civil trial opens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) civil suit against Datuk Seri Najib Razak opened today, with the state investment fund alleging that the former prime minister orchestrated a "top-down" fraud that caused losses of about RM51.4 billion and abused his positions to direct the company's affairs. The plaintiffs, comprising 1MDB and four of its subsidiaries, alleged that Najib exploited his positions as prime minister, finance minister and chairman of 1MDB's board of advisers to direct the company's affairs. Lim said the alleged losses comprised US$1.83 billion in the Good Star phase, US$1.367 billion in the Aabar phase, US$1.591 billion in the Tanore phase and US$856.3 million in the Options Buyback phase.

items.title: State Speaker: Selangor assembly reviewing all lawmakers after bankruptcy disqualification claim
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 3 — The Selangor state assembly is reviewing the status of all its members after claims that one assemblyman may have been disqualified over bankruptcy, Utusan Malaysia reported today. State assembly Speaker Lau Weng San said he could not yet confirm the identity of the lawmaker concerned because checks and investigations were still under way. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari previously said the matter would be determined by Lau before the Election Commission (EC) was informed.

items.title: Cook charged with assaulting fiancée-to-be with helmet
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A 22-year-old cook was charged at the magistrate's court here with assaulting his fiancée-to-be using a helmet after she allegedly went out with another man. The accused, Amyrul Fitri Rahshidi Rosman, 22, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. According to the charge, he allegedly injured his 22-year-old fiancée-to-be using a helmet at the Batu Pahat market here at 3.30pm on July 30.

items.title: Religious affairs minister to table Tabung Haji RCI findings in Dewan Rakyat next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will present the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji (TH) at a special parliamentary sitting next week. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the special sitting, scheduled for Aug 11, was called under Standing Order 14(1)(i). Last Thursday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said that the special sitting would be held next Monday following agreement from the Dewan Rakyat Speaker.

items.title: Malaysia targets rail cable theft with possible RM100,000 fines and 1,146 new CCTV cameras, Dewan Negara told
items.summary: Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the proposal to increase the fine from the current RM1,000 is expected to be tabled in the next Parliament session. Additionally, the move was also driven by a surge in cable theft cases which recorded a total loss of RM50 million across the Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) network, Prasarana Malaysia Berhad and the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project. “This brings the total loss to RM4.75 million.

items.title: Woman killed, son injured after Toyota Avanza crashes into guardrail in Kedah
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 3 — A woman was killed while her son was injured after the vehicle they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a roadside guardrail along Jalan Batu Pengasah in Durian Burung, near Padang Terap, today. Padang Terap police chief Supt Mohd Anuar Junoh said the incident, which occurred at about 7.35am, claimed the life of the 55-year-old woman, who was seated in the front passenger seat. “Preliminary investigations found that the victims were travelling from Kuala Nerang towards Durian Burung when the vehicle skidded onto the left road shoulder before crashing into the roadside guardrail.

items.title: Cambodian DPM Prak Sokhonn arrives in Malaysia for two-day official visit
items.summary: SEPANG, Aug 3 — Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Prak Sokhonn arrived in Malaysia today for a two-day official visit. Sokhonn is also expected to hold bilateral talks with Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. Malaysia and Cambodia recorded robust trade growth in 2025, with bilateral trade rising 27.4 per cent year-on-year to RM5 billion (US$1.17 billion).

items.title: Alibaba unveils its most capable AI model to date, not far behind Moonshot's in size
items.summary: Chinese tech companies — a huge force in open-weight AI models globally — are locked in a fierce and fast-moving battle to build more powerful systems without making them prohibitively expensive to run. Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4 trillion parameters, the numerical settings a model learns from data and uses to recognise patterns, generate answers, and carry out tasks. Moonshot's Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters.

items.title: Man pleads not guilty to robbing security guard of shotgun outside Klang bank
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 3 — A man pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of armed robbery last month. Ahmad Shukri Suhairin, 24, was accused of robbing a 51-year-old man at gunpoint and taking a pump gun belonging to a security company in front of a bank in Bandar Bukit Tinggi here at 5.45 pm on July 20. Deputy public prosecutor Nor Suhaili Abu Bakar proposed bail of RM10,000 with suitable conditions.

items.title: Xin Hwa faces going concern warning from auditor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Xin Hwa Holdings Bhd has come under a going concern warning after its external auditor flagged material uncertainty over its ability to continue operating, with current liabilities exceeding current assets. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, Xin Hwa said PKF PLT had issued a modified audit opinion highlighting the going concern uncertainty in its audit of the company's financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026. Additionally, Xin Hwa said it had significantly reduced and deferred non-crucial capital expenditure during the current financial year.

items.title: Malaysia’s private sector encouraged to play bigger role in helping PwDs reach their potential, says deputy minister
items.summary: Also present were Penang Social Welfare Department director Rozita Ibrahim and Petron head of Retail Business Shaliza Mohd Sidek. Lim expressed hope that the strategic collaboration between the Social Welfare Department (JKM), Seberang Jaya PPDK and the corporate sector, including Petron service station operators in Penang, would serve as a model and inspire more private companies to contribute towards improving the well-being of PwDs. She said the RM62,400 initiative was fully funded by Petron service station operators in Penang without any financial contribution from the JKM.

items.title: Thailand tightens border security after Tak Bai shootout
items.summary: TUMPAT: Thai authorities have tightened security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following a shootout in Tak Bai yesterday that left two policemen dead and three others injured. "Soon after the incident, I directed border agencies to step up security operations along our border with Malaysia. "Security personnel have been instructed to strengthen surveillance and block possible escape routes, particularly along the border," he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Umno chief dismisses speculation over absence from new MB’s swearing-in
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has dismissed speculation that his absence from the swearing-in of the state’s new menteri besar reflected disappointment over the appointment, saying the invitation arrived only at 4.50am and clashed with an earlier engagement. Jalaluddin, who New Straits Times (NST) reported was believed to have been among those considered for the post, said he read the invitation from the state protocol unit after Subuh prayers. Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim was sworn in as menteri besar before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Govt finalising rail law amendments to raise cable theft fines to RM100,000
items.summary: Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the proposal to increase the fine from the current RM1,000 is expected to be tabled in the next parliamentary session. The move was also driven by a surge in cable theft cases, which recorded total losses of RM50 million across the Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) network, Prasarana Malaysia Bhd, and the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project. According to Hasbi, a total of 71 cable theft cases were recorded along the ECRL project with an estimated loss of RM4.06 million, while 13 cases of theft and equipment damage resulted in losses of RM0.69 million.

items.title: Couple charged with abusing 9-year-old daughter
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A lorry driver and his wife pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to charges of abusing their 9-year-old daughter, leaving her with swelling, bruises, welts and trauma. The accused, aged 36 and 35, entered their pleas before judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah after the charges were read to them. The male accused was charged with physically abusing his daughter at a house in Presint Selendang, Taman 1 Krubong, Melaka Tengah, at 7pm on July 19.

items.title: US reaffirms commitment to rule of law in Indo-Pacific
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States remains committed to sharing common legal values and principles with its allies and partners in the Indo-Pacific region to protect sovereign equality, safeguard sovereign rights and advance the interests of all nations. US Pacific Command (USPACOM) Staff Judge Advocate Captain Dustin Wallace said the United States and its partners, including Asean countries, viewed the rule of law as a means to safeguard and protect rights, rather than using law as a tool to isolate, intimidate or coerce other nations. "We at USPACOM are firmly committed to the rule of law, ensuring that we use our legal, shared legal values and shared legal principles with our allies and partners to protect sovereign equality, safeguard sovereign rights and advance the interests of all our nations," he said at a press conference held in conjunction with the USPACOM 37th International Military Law and Operations Conference (Milops) 2026 today.

items.title: Deputy transport minister: Rail cable theft costs Malaysia RM50m since 2024, causes 381 hours of KTMB delays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Cable theft across Malaysia’s railway network has caused RM50.05 million in losses since 2024 and led to 381 hours of delays to KTMB services in 2025 alone, the Transport Ministry said today. KTMB recorded 432 cases between 2024 and June this year, involving an estimated 19,756 metres of cable and losses of about RM16.3 million. Hasbi said Prasarana recorded 163 cable theft cases involving the MRT and LRT networks, with estimated losses reaching RM29 million.

items.title: Teenager pleads guilty to abandoning newborn in bushes
items.summary: TAWAU: A 15-year-old school dropout pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court here today to abandoning her newborn baby in bushes at Kampung Jawa Sentosa, Jalan Guru, last month. According to the charge, she allegedly abandoned her newborn girl with the intention of dumping the child in bushes at Kampung Jawa Sentosa, Jalan Guru, at 4.30am on July 21. Based on the facts of the case, police received public information at 7am on July 21 regarding the discovery of a newborn baby girl beside a house near the SMK Tawau Teachers' Flat in Kampung Jawa.

items.title: Murder trial begins for 15-year-old accused of fatally stabbing schoolmate in Bandar Utama
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The murder trial of a 15-year-old boy accused of fatally stabbing his 16-year-old schoolmate in a girls’ toilet at a Bandar Utama school in Petaling Jaya began today, with the victim’s mother and the pathologist who conducted the post-mortem among those expected to testify. According to New Straits Times , the prosecution is expected to call 11 witnesses during the eight-day trial before High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid. According to the charge sheet, the boy is accused of murdering Form Four student Yap Shing Xuen in the girls’ toilet of SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4) in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, between 9.20am and 9.35am on October 14 last year.

items.title: Jealousy lands lorry driver in court for assaulting wife
items.summary: Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno questioned the accused on where he would stay if bail was granted, stressing that he could not live with his wife while the case was ongoing. "If the court allows bail, where will you stay? The accused told the court he would stay at his parents' house until the case was concluded.

items.title: Jalaluddin clarifies absence at Negri Sembilan MB swearing-in ceremony
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has clarified that his absence at the menteri besar swearing-in ceremony at Istana Besar Seri Menanti yesterday was due to short notice. Jalaluddin, who is the Pertang assemblyman, said he received the invitation from the state Protocol unit at 4.50am. Yesterday, Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim took his oath as the new Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Five Taiwanese charged with trafficking Cameroonian woman for forced labour
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Five Taiwanese citizens pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a human trafficking charge involving a Cameroonian woman for alleged forced labour last month. The accused — Chien Te Hsi, 27; Liao Shao Wei, 36; Hung Min Hung, 35; Chao Jhih Ying, 35; and Tseng Wei Ting, 29 — entered their pleas before judge Roslan Hamid after the charge was read to them in Mandarin by a court interpreter. They were charged with trafficking a Cameroonian woman for forced labour at a premises in Jalan Utara Berapit, Central Seberang Perai, at 7pm on July 16.

items.title: Chow: Penang PH to stay focused on governance
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) will remain focused on governing the state despite Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional's confidence in capturing Penang. State PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the opposition was entitled to pursue its own electoral strategy, but the outcome would ultimately depend on voters. Chow, who is also Penang Chief Minister, said PH in Penang would continue to champion inclusive governance and development for all communities instead of engaging in identity-based politics.

items.title: Terengganu police deny preferential treatment for RXZ Members 8.0, citing six arrests and 1,850 summonses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Terengganu police have denied giving preferential treatment to the organisers or participants of RXZ Members 8.0, pointing to arrests and summonses issued during the motorcycle gathering as evidence that the law was enforced. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said the force had remained professional throughout the event and rejected claims that those involved had received “special treatment”, Sinar Harian reported. “As for the claim that the police gave participants ‘special treatment’, I do not think so.

items.title: SunCon lands RM1.02bil Johor data centre job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) has secured a RM1.02 billion contract for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works of a data centre development in Johor. SunCon, in a Bursa Malaysia filing today, said its subsidiary Sunway Construction Sdn Bhd had accepted a letter of award from a US-headquartered multinational technology corporation for the project. SunCon said the contract is expected to contribute to the group's earnings from the financial year 2026 onwards.

items.title: US committed to strengthening defence ties with Malaysia - Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States will continue strengthening its close relations with Malaysia, including in the defence sector, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. "They said they will continue to give further attention to enhancing and strengthening the close relations between the two countries, including in the defence sector," he said when met after the meeting. He said the defence sector played an important role in supporting Asean's objectives and enhancing cooperation among member states.

items.title: Selangor demolishes 72 illegal factories on government land, majority in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 3 — A total of 72 factories operating on government land have been demolished this year, with 53 of them located within the administrative areas of the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) and the Petaling District and Land Office. Selangor Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said another 19 factories demolished through a special operation were located within the areas under the Royal Klang City Council (MDBK) and the Klang District and Land Office (PDT). “This is also part of the enforcement process against land use that does not comply with stated conditions, encroachment on government land or the operation of unauthorised factories (KTK),” he said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly session today.

items.title: FT minister turns to Selangor for retention ponds as KL runs out of land
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today she plans to meet Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to discuss developing more retention ponds outside Kuala Lumpur, as the capital has little land left for new flood mitigation projects. Selangor has land, so let’s get this conversation together,” she said. Yeoh said the shortage of available land in Kuala Lumpur had forced City Hall to adopt alternative approaches, including constructing underground retention ponds beneath public parks.

items.title: Mother, boyfriend charged with murdering 5-year-old boy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: An Indonesian woman and her Bangladeshi boyfriend were charged in the magistrate's court here today with murdering a 5-year-old boy. The victim was the Indonesian woman's son with her Rohingya husband, who died last year. Sany, 34, and Dina Hayati, 30, nodded to indicate they understood the charge read before magistrate Noor Idayu Salim.

items.title: Malaysia weighing limited return of raw rare-earth exports amid growing foreign interest, deputy minister says
items.summary: Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said authorities were assessing whether to ease the restrictions amid pressure from state governments and investors. Syed Ibrahim said any renewed exports would be tied to investment in Malaysia and technology transfers, and should be used for research and development overseas. “Diversification is particularly important,” Syed Ibrahim said.

items.title: Nestle Malaysia beats 2025 emissions goal ahead of schedule
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has reduced its greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) by 31 per cent from its 2018 baseline. Nestle Malaysia said the achievement was driven by initiatives across its operations and supply chain. Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the milestone reflected years of collaboration across the company's operations and value chain.

items.title: Amir Hamzah says Budi95 shields citizens, more than 14.2 million enjoy targeted fuel aid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — More than 14.2 million out of 16.7 million people who are eligible for the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidy have benefitted from the programme, involving the consumption of more than 13.4 billion litres of RON95 fuel, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah explained that, based on the current implementation, annual fiscal savings are estimated at between RM2.5 billion and RM4.0 billion, subject to global crude oil prices, exchange rate movements, and actual fuel consumption patterns. Responding to a supplementary question from Senator Robert Lau Hui Yew regarding the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) recommendation that Malaysia gradually phase out Budi95 and adopt other policy mechanisms over the medium term, Amir Hamzah said the government has already shifted to a targeted subsidy system from the previous blanket fuel subsidy.

items.title: 14.2 million Malaysians benefit from targeted RON95 subsidy, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 14.2 million of the 16.7 million eligible Malaysians have benefited from the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) targeted fuel subsidy programme, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said the initiative involved the consumption of over 13.4 billion litres of RON95 fuel. Amir Hamzah explained that based on current implementation, annual fiscal savings are estimated at between RM2.5 billion and RM4.0 billion, depending on global crude oil prices, exchange rate movements, and fuel consumption patterns.

items.title: Prosecution objects to Daim’s daughter’s stay bid in undeclared shareholdings case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The prosecution has objected to the application by the daughter of the late former Finance Minister Tun Daim Zainuddin for a stay of proceedings in her case, which involves charges of failing to declare shareholdings in five companies in 2023. Earlier, Asnida Abdul Daim’s counsel Muhammad Nizamuddin Abdul Hamid filed the application to refer several questions of law to the Federal Court, on the grounds that they involve legal issues similar to those in the case of the late minister’s widow, Toh Puan Na’imah Abdul Khalid, who faces charges of failing to declare her assets. The shareholdings in question involve five companies: Amiraz Sdn Bhd, Arida Farms Sdn Bhd, Kangkung Catering Sdn Bhd, Transgrade Sdn Bhd and Gajah3 Foods Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Teenager's murder trial over Bandar Utama school stabbing begins
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The murder trial of a 15-year-old boy accused of fatally stabbing his schoolmate at a school in Bandar Utama last year begins today. The prosecution is expected to call the pathologist who conducted the 16-year-old victim's post-mortem examination as its first witness. Several teachers from the school are among the witnesses expected to take the stand today.

items.title: Azalina: BN-Perikatan alliance not fixed, cooperation depends on political landscape in each state
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 3 — Barisan Nasional (BN) leader Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that her coalition’s alliance with Perikatan Nasional (PN) was not a fixed arrangement and that any cooperation would hinge on the local political landscape. BN and PN teamed up again in the Negeri Sembilan polls on Saturday, securing more than a two-thirds majority in the state assembly to oust the two-term PH government. It was the second major blow to the coalition led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim after the Johor state election.

items.title: Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official, government says
items.summary: BANGKOK: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, a government spokeswoman said, amid concerns over the health of the 81-year-old. Since then, Suu Kyi's exact whereabouts and health condition have been difficult to determine, with no foreign leader or envoy having publicly met her. On Monday, Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw, government spokeswoman Khine Khine Soe said in a message via Telegram.

items.title: Penang Pakatan to discuss election strategy and Umno’s role in state government on Aug 8, says Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 3 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) will discuss Umno’s position in the state government at a meeting on August 8 as it steps up preparations for the next general or state election, state PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said today. “I believe the issue of Umno or Barisan Nasional’s position in the Penang state government will also be discussed at that meeting,” the Penang chief minister said. Chow said the performance of PH’s component parties apart from DAP would also be among the topics discussed at the state PH meeting.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow: Pakatan won’t play racial politics in Penang fight
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 3 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will not resort to racial or identity-based politics in its bid to retain Penang, said Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow. The Penang chief minister said the coalition would continue to seek support through its record of inclusive governance and development. Responding to questions on whether identity politics employed by Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) could gain traction in Penang, Chow said PH remains committed to governing for all communities.

items.title: Amirudin urges fair debate over Selangor stray dog issue
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has urged all parties not to be selective in criticising the state government over the stray dog issue, stressing the need to balance public safety and animal welfare. He said the state government would continue taking action against stray dogs but must consider the wider public interest. Amirudin said the focus should be on finding a balance by preventing stray dogs from roaming freely and posing risks to residents, while also addressing animal welfare concerns.

items.title: KL reforms take time, Hannah Yeoh says contracts and costs block quick fixes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh today said reforms to improve Kuala Lumpur’s liveability cannot happen overnight, as even seemingly simple changes require negotiations with multiple stakeholders, existing contracts, and financial considerations. “Everything takes time, right? Because every single thing has a contract involved.

items.title: Trump attorney-general pick says has reached deal with senators after standoff
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US acting attorney general said on Sunday he had reached an agreement with lawmakers and issued an order officially scrapping a US$1.8 billion compensation fund that had led to a standoff over his Senate confirmation. Todd Blanche's announcement came after the Senate Judiciary Committee pushed back a vote on advancing his nomination owing to his continuing dispute with Republican Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina. A signed order attached to Blanche's post said: "The Attorney General's May 18, 2026 Order establishing the Anti-Weaponisation Fund... is rescinded and shall have no force or effect.

items.title: BHEUU targets faster legal reforms, better access to justice
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Accelerating legal reform, digital transformation and improving access to justice are among key priorities under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister's Department Strategic Plan 2026-2030. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the roadmap was designed to position BHEUU as a leading force in legal and institutional reform to support national wellbeing. Azalina said the plan focused on three key priorities including driving responsive legal reforms, strengthening the implementation and delivery of legislation, and enhancing digital capabilities through technology, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI).

items.title: Maybank buys remaining Ageas stake for RM4.83bil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is buying the remaining 30.95 per cent stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd from Ageas Insurance International NV for RM4.83 billion. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Maybank said it had entered into an implementation agreement with Ageas for the proposed acquisition, which is subject to approval from Bank Negara Malaysia. The bank said the acquisition is expected to strengthen Maybank Ageas' position as a national insurance and takaful champion while providing greater flexibility to expand across Southeast Asia.

items.title: Azalina calls for agile legal framework amid AI and digital challenges
items.summary: hakimmahari@nst.com.my PUTRAJAYA: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation and cybersecurity threats require Malaysia's legal framework to become more agile, responsive and future-ready, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said the changing global landscape had created new challenges that required continuous improvements in laws and institutions. She said legal reforms were no longer limited to introducing or amending legislation, but also involved ensuring public institutions remained trusted, effective and capable of responding to emerging challenges.

items.title: Selangor MB reveals locals shielding Rohingya, warns collusion obstructs enforcement efforts
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 3 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has revealed that some locals are believed to be protecting illegal immigrants, including Rohingya, making enforcement efforts more challenging. He said the existence of inappropriate collusion between certain local residents and the groups involved was among the factors preventing authorities from taking effective action. He was replying to a question from Datuk Johan Abd Aziz (BN-Dusun Tua) on issues involving illegal immigrants and Rohingya in Hulu Langat.

items.title: Terengganu police chief: Five deaths, 1,850 summonses and 222 motorcycles seized during RXZ Members 8.0 gathering
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Five people were killed in road accidents during the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering in Terengganu, as the number of crashes recorded over the event period nearly tripled from last year. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said five fatal accident cases were recorded this year, compared with two cases last year. Police recorded four criminal cases during this year’s gathering, compared with six during RXZ Members 7.0 last year.

items.title: No pilgrims remain in Saudi Arabia under Haj operations, consulate urges public to ignore rumours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Consulate General of Malaysia in Jeddah on Sunday denied claims circulating on social media that Malaysian Haj pilgrims were still in Saudi Arabia under the management of the 1447H/2026 Haj season. In a statement, the consulate general said all Malaysian haj pilgrims for the 1447H/2026 Haj season had safely returned home according to the schedule set by the Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji). “There are no Malaysian haj pilgrims remaining in Saudi Arabia under the 1447H/2026 Haj operations,” the statement said.

items.title: Public rushes to rescue three after car reverses into Padas River in Beaufort
items.summary: BEAUFORT, Aug 3 — A 28-year-old male driver, a 29-year-old female passenger, and a 10-year-old child escaped unhurt when their car plunged into the Padas River behind Maybank here on Saturday. Beaufort Fire and Rescue Station chief Ishak Jabas confirmed the incident on Sunday, stating that the station received an emergency call at 8.42pm. A seven-member team equipped with a CFRT vehicle and a Vigo pickup truck was dispatched to the scene located two kilometres away, where a Perodua Bezza had backed into the river while reversing.

items.title: Tuan Ibrahim: PAS ready for talks on extending BN-Perikatan cooperation to Melaka and federal level
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — PAS is prepared to discuss extending the Barisan Nasional (BN)-Perikatan Nasional (PN) cooperation model used in Negeri Sembilan to the Melaka state election and potentially to the federal level, its deputy president has said. Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the results of the cooperation in Negeri Sembilan had been very encouraging and provided a basis for further discussions on its future, Harian Metro reported. “We saw that the cooperation in Negeri Sembilan produced very good results and achievements.

items.title: Rosmah seeks fresh evidence in solar corruption appeal, claims witness was pressured to implicate her
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has asked the Court of Appeal to admit fresh evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case, alleging that a prosecution witness was pressured into giving evidence that incriminated her, FMT reported. In an affidavit supporting the application, Rosmah claimed that prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah had been pressured into giving incriminating evidence during her High Court trial. Rosmah is also seeking permission to recall Rayyan to give further evidence before either the Court of Appeal or the High Court.

items.title: Technician pleads not guilty to reckless driving over Pahang crash that killed doctor, his two-year-old daughter and another motorist
items.summary: Syed Muhammad Izzar Aiman Syed Ahmad, 31, claimed trial after the charge was read before magistrate Melody Woon Sze Mun in Pekan today, Sinar Harian reported. He is accused of driving an Isuzu D-MAX four-wheel-drive vehicle recklessly and causing the deaths of Dr Mohamad Zekry Zuhairy Mohd Atan, 33, his daughter Dhea Sofia, two, and Azaharuddin Mohd Ali, 46. Syed Muhammad Izzar was charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Selangor assembly to clarify lawmaker’s status this week after reported bankruptcy, says Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Selangor state assembly is expected to clarify this week whether an unnamed assemblyman has lost his seat after reportedly being declared bankrupt, Utusan Malaysia reported. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the matter would be determined by the state assembly Speaker, Lau Weng San, before the Election Commission (EC) was formally informed. But I believe the state assembly will prepare a note, and I think that by this week at the latest, we will announce the status of the assemblyman concerned,” Amirudin said today.
